name: QuillBot
tagline: AI paraphrasing, grammar, summarization, and writing tools

pricing.notes: Official pricing/FAQ checked 2026-07-30; monthly Premium listed at $19.95, quarterly $13.31/month, annual $8.33/month.

verdictSummary: A paraphraser/summarizer/grammar wrapper over an LLM and LanguageTool is easy to build; the paid app wins on UX, extensions, plagiarism workflows, and bundled tools.
coreLoopDIY: Create text boxes for paraphrase/summarize/grammar, call an LLM and LanguageTool, and save/export outputs.
requirements: browser extension if in-app writing is needed
whyPeopleStillPay: They pay because it is available where they write and has purpose-built controls.

priorArt.name: LanguageTool

alternatives.name: Apple Writing Tools
alternatives.desc: Proofread, rewrite, shorten, or change tone almost anywhere, assuming your Apple hardware made the guest list.

alternatives.name: Page Assist
alternatives.desc: A browser sidebar that reads the page, rewrites the selection, and saves custom actions; your local model does the thinking.

alternatives.name: Witsy
alternatives.desc: System-wide selected-text commands, reusable experts, a scratchpad, and document context; bring the model and skip the subscription.

alternatives.name: Writing Tools
alternatives.desc: Select text anywhere, hit a hotkey, and fix, rewrite, summarize, or obey a custom instruction without opening another tab.

notes: Great yes candidate: wrapper-heavy, high willingness to cancel.
prompt:
Build me a local paraphrasing and grammar tool to replace QuillBot. Requirements:

- A local web page on localhost:5170: Node + Express, one textarea in, one output pane,
  buttons for Paraphrase, Summarize, Fix grammar, and a tone select (standard, formal,
  casual, shorter).
- Paraphrase, summarize, and tone modes call an LLM (Anthropic or OpenAI key in .env)
  with a fixed prompt per mode; stream the output.
- Grammar mode calls a local LanguageTool server and lists each issue with its suggested
  fix, click to apply. No LLM needed for grammar.
- A diff view between input and output with word-level highlights (the `diff` npm
  package).
- Every run saved to SQLite via better-sqlite3: timestamp, mode, input, output. A
  history page lists the last 100 with copy buttons.
- Cmd+Enter runs the selected mode.
- No accounts, no telemetry; text leaves my machine only for LLM calls, grammar checking
  stays fully local.
- Out of scope: browser and Word extensions, plagiarism and AI detection. This lives in
  one tab.
- README: LanguageTool setup (needs Java or Docker) and which API key to add.
